one_line: A 29-second top-down kitchen demo that says do not give kids strawberries before soaking them in water and vinegar, shows the soak, shows dark specks in the poured-out water, and ends on a clean strawberry that is ok to serve.

hook.visual: A white bowl on a wooden table seen from above; a leaf falls in at 0.0 s and strawberries are dropped into the bowl one after another over the first 3 seconds.
hook.on_screen_text: אל תתנו לילדים תותים לפני שאתם עושים את זה (Do not give children strawberries before you do this)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: it opens with a prohibition about children and food, in a text box over a pretty, simple image, and withholds what 'this' is. The viewer must watch to the end to learn the step, and the fear of getting it wrong is personal for any parent.

beats.observed: Empty white bowl, then strawberries are placed in one by one on a wood surface, shot from directly above.
beats.on_screen_text: אל תתנו לילדים תותים לפני שאתם עושים את זה (Do not give children strawberries before you do this)

beats.observed: A full bowl of strawberries, unchanged.
beats.on_screen_text: תותים הם מסוג הפירות שמקבלים הכי הרבה ריסוס (Strawberries are the type of fruit that gets sprayed the most)

beats.observed: Water is poured over the strawberries in the bowl (7.5 s); a branded 5% vinegar bottle is held up (10.5 s); the bowl is shown again filled with strawberries and water.
beats.on_screen_text: שטיפה במים לא תסיר מהם את חומרי ההדברה (Rinsing with water will not remove the pesticides from them), then at 9.0 s: השרייה במים עם שתי כפות חומץ (Soaking in water with two tablespoons of vinegar)

beats.observed: Vinegar from a red-capped bottle is poured into the bowl of strawberries and water.
beats.on_screen_text: תנקה אותם מכל השאריות של החומרים (It will clean them of all the residues of the substances)

beats.observed: The strawberries are tipped into a metal strainer and the liquid is poured out into another white bowl.
beats.on_screen_text: Same line carries to 16.5 s, then no text.

beats.observed: Close-up of the poured-out water in a white bowl with many tiny dark specks suspended in it.
beats.on_screen_text: תראו מה יצא מההשרייה (Look what came out of the soaking)

beats.observed: The strawberries in the strainer are rinsed under running tap water.
A hand with red nail polish holds one clean, glossy strawberry in extreme close-up over the sink.
beats.on_screen_text: עכשיו שהסרנו מהם את שאריות חומרי ההדברה (Now that we have removed the pesticide residues from them). Then: אפשר להגיש אותם לילדים (They can be served to children)

payoff: The method (water plus two tablespoons of vinegar) is shown at about 7.5-10.5 s; the 'proof' of dirty water arrives at 19.5-21.0 s; the safe-to-serve verdict and the clean strawberry arrive at 24-29 s, the very end.
cta: None in the video. The caption restates the rule (soak for 10 minutes in water and vinegar) and ends with a reassurance line; there is no explicit save or share request.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: a parent who gives strawberries to a child will save it as a kitchen rule and send it to partners and grandparents. The dirty-water shot also invites reactions. The 371 comments could include doubts about the claim, but comment content is not in the data.
why_it_worked: 886,741 views on an account with a median of 859 views (outlier_x 1,032): the topic, not the account's following, carried it, and a parent-safety warning is broadly relevant (inferred).
The hook is a mistake or prohibition, and its answer is delayed to the last 5 seconds, which pushes viewers to watch to the end (observed from the timeline).
like_rate 0.82% is healthy, and the single visual proof moment (dark specks in the water at 19.5 s) makes the method feel real (observed).
paid_signal: unclear | like_rate 0.82% is above the 0.3% flag, so there is no direct paid sign, but a 1,032x outlier on an account with a median of 859 views is extreme, so a boost cannot be ruled out. This is inference only.

solo_route.how: 1) Mount a phone directly above a table (a stack of books and a tripod or clip works) and use a plain bowl and natural light. 2) Choose one 'do not do X before you do this' rule from LumeBook's own FAQ or likeness pillar and film a single-take, 25-second demo of the correct way. 3) Add Canva or CapCut text boxes in a rounded white label style, one idea per box, and no voice-over needed. 4) Withhold the verdict (the answer or the final preview) until the last 4-5 seconds.
solo_route.needs: Nothing, but do not copy the pesticide or health claim: it is not verified by anything in the video, and the water specks might not be pesticide.

lumebook_version.hook_he: אל תעלו תמונה של הילד לספר לפני שעשיתם את זה (Do not upload your child's photo to the book before you do this)
lumebook_version.concept: Screen recording plus overhead phone shot: a parent's phone, three quick checks (face fully visible, even light, no sunglasses or hats), then the last 5 seconds reveal the LumeBook preview of the child as the hero, side by side with the weaker preview from a bad photo, which makes the checklist worth saving.

evidence_notes: Observed: the full sequence of text boxes, the pour, the vinegar bottle and the tiny dark specks in the poured-out water. Spoken: the Whisper transcript is only "תודה רבה." over 29 s and is a hallucination or music-only, so there is no usable speech transcript. Inferred: the safety anxiety, the share motive and the paid-signal reasoning. Not verified: that the specks are pesticide residue (they could be dirt, seeds or other particles), that vinegar soaking removes 'almost all' residues as the caption claims, and that strawberries are the most sprayed fruit. The account is a wooden-toys and Montessori store, so the clip is off-product content that behaved like a creator health tip. Only a hand with red nail polish is visible; no face is shown and no one is identified.
